title: Egress masquerade + MTU/PMTU fallback incident (scratchpad)
content:
Summary:

On 2024-11-12 we observed intermittent egress failures from pods to external services (HTTP downstreams timing out, TLS handshakes failing). The failure surface was only on certain zones and node pools running a specific instance type and kernel. Symptoms pointed to path MTU/fragmentation issues combined with iptables MASQUERADE behaviour: large packets were dropped, TCP retransmit patterns caused conntrack table entries to balloon, and kube-proxy/iptables SNAT rules did not properly handle fragments in our overlay.

Impact:
- ~3% of pods in eu-west-2 experienced transient outbound failures between 09:10 and 11:40 UTC.
- Customer-facing retries masked some errors but increased tail latency and request cost.
- A handful of long-lived connections (gRPC) were permanently disrupted requiring pod restarts.

Initial detection and triage notes (timeline):
- 09:12 UTC: Pager triggered for elevated client error rate to external billing service (alerts from service-level SLO monitor).
- 09:18 UTC: On-call verified errors were HTTP 504/timeout and TLS handshake errors; internal service-to-service calls not impacted.
- 09:25 UTC: Netflow/dashboard showed high TCP retransmit ratio originating from pods on node-pool-3b.
- 09:35 UTC: tcpdump on affected node captured ICMP "fragmentation needed" (Type 3, Code 4) messages from upstream router. PMTU discovery appeared to be failing to adjust.
- 09:50 UTC: Conntrack entries for SNAT flows increased significantly; conntrack table nearing soft limit on affected nodes.
- 10:05 UTC: Temporary mitigation rolled — set net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max to a higher value on affected nodes and restarted kube-proxy (not ideal; riskier) — immediate drop in new drop rate but symptoms resumed under load.
- 10:40 UTC: Confirmed correlation with instance type using older kernel and host GSO/GRO settings that do not handle fragmented overlay packets well.
- 11:00 UTC: Full mitigation: standardize MTU to 1400 on host ENIs of affected pool (matching overlay+encap overhead) and roll a controlled node restart with updated kernel sysctl for GRO/GSO off. Errors returned to baseline by 11:40 UTC.

Hypotheses and root cause (working):
1) Underlay MTU + overlay encapsulation mismatch led to packets larger than path MTU.
2) Upstream router returns ICMP "fragmentation needed" but either ICMP is filtered somewhere or PMTU discovery failed because packets were TCP segmented with GSO/GRO and not triggering the expected ICMP behaviour to the sender.
3) Because fragments weren't handled/passed through correctly by the host or CNI, kube-proxy's SNAT translation produced conntrack entries for half-open/failed flows, causing table growth and CPU pressure when conntrack garbage collection kicked in.
4) Some kernels on the instance family had a bug/optimization with offloads that dropped ICMP fragments or failed to coalesce correctly under VXLAN/Geneve, which made the observable symptom node-pool-specific.

Immediate mitigation steps (bullet runbook for on-call):
- Identify affected nodes: kubectl get nodes -l pool=node-pool-3b and cross-check kernel version (uname -r) and ethtool -k for GSO/GRO settings.
- Check for ICMP type 3 code 4 in tcpdump: tcpdump -i any -vvv icmp and filter src/dst. If ICMP present but PMTU not adapting, check that iptables is not dropping ICMP (iptables -S | grep icmp).
- Temporarily set host MTU to conservative value that accommodates overlay encapsulation: ip link set dev eth0 mtu 1400 (or cluster standard mtu minus encapsulation overhead). Roll this via a cordon/drain/rotate strategy for nodes.
- Disable GSO/GRO on host as a quick mitigation for boxes with suspect offload behavior: ethtool -K eth0 gso off gro off tso off. Note: this reduces throughput; document CPU impact.
- If conntrack table is near limit: sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144 and increase nf_conntrack_buckets accordingly. Restart kube-proxy only after draining node or during safe window.
- Short-term firewall rule: allow ICMP fragmentation-needed messages through perimeter filters to ensure PMTU discovery can complete.

Commands to collect forensic evidence (on affected node):
- uname -a
- ethtool -k eth0
- ip link show
- ip route show table all
- sysctl net.ipv4.route.flush (only if testing changes)
- ss -tn state established sport = :443 or dst X.Y.Z.W to find stuck flows
- sudo conntrack -L | wc -l and sudo conntrack -L | grep <external-ip> to inspect flows
- sudo tcpdump -n -s 0 -w /tmp/egress.pcap host <external-ip> and icmp

Monitoring/alerts to add/change (longer-term):
- Add per-node metric: conntrack.count and conntrack.max with alert when > 70% of capacity for > 5m.
- Track TCP retransmit ratio per-node and SRE team alert when per-node retransmit > 5% and RPS to external services > threshold.
- Create a dashboard showing PMTU-related ICMP (if available), overlay MTU mismatch (host MTU vs overlay MTU), and kernel versions by node pool.

Post-incident remediation and follow-ups (owners assigned):
- infra: Bake host MTU and ethtool offload settings into node image for node-pool-3b (owner: Marcos Rivera).
- platform: Add preflight check during node scale-up to validate MTU compatibility between host ENI and CNI overlay (owner: Aisha Patel).
- infra/oss: Investigate kernel/instance type bug for GSO/GRO with VXLAN/Geneve and file upstream bug if confirmed (owner: Sofia Ivanov).
- product: Communicate customer-facing RCA summary for impacted customers (owner: Liam Chen).
- SRE: Implement conntrack observability and alerts (owner: Liam Chen).

RCA notes (to iterate into formal postmortem):
- Primary contributing factor: mismatch between configured MTU and actual path MTU after overlay encapsulation; exacerbated by host offload behavior.
- Secondary: partial filtering or improper handling of ICMP fragmentation-needed messages in our perimeter or intermediate routers, breaking PMTU discovery.
- Tertiary: conntrack/table pressure and kube-proxy restarts masked the root cause by producing cascading failures under load.

Open questions / things to validate:
- Which router/firewall (cloud-managed) along the path is dropping or altering ICMP messages? Do we have a packet capture at the VPC boundary?
- Is there an init script or cloud-agent on the older instance image that toggles offload flags on boot?
- Can we instrument PMTU discovery success rate end-to-end from a synthetic probe in each AZ?

Draft runbook for "egress large-packet failure":
1) Alert triggers: client egress error rate or TCP retransmit ratio spike.
2) Query nodes with high retransmit and conntrack pressure.
3) Verify ICMP type 3 presence; if none, check perimeter firewall rules.
4) If ICMP present and packets > MTU, set conservative MTU on host and disable offloads for verification.
5) If conntrack near capacity, increase nf_conntrack_max and rotate nodes (drain, restart kube-proxy after node reboot).
6) After remediation, schedule rolling fix via image bake and cluster-autoscaler config to ensure new nodes are compliant.

Notes to self (informal):
- This incident felt noisy because of mixed signals: conntrack GC CPU spikes made us think conntrack was primary instead of symptom.
- Need a small synthetic that attempts to POST ~8k payloads from pods to an external echo server to surface PMTU failures continuously.
- Be cautious with ethtool toggles; in our benchmarks disabling GSO/GRO moves CPU utilization up ~10-20% on busy nodes.

Related artifacts and drafts:
- Draft PR to node-image repo to set mtu=1400 and disable gso/gro for node-pool-3b (WIP) — see linked commit.
- Slack thread for live debugging: #sre-egress-2024-11-12 

Next steps (short):
- Finish image bake and schedule gradual rollout to node-pool-3b (Marcos).
- Add conntrack + retransmit alerts and dashboard (Liam).
- Run PMTU synthetic checks from each zone (Aisha).

End of scratchpad.

(Will convert to formal incident review once follow-ups have clear telemetry and PRs merged.)
